rules.insideEphemerisSpan: The moment lies from 1800 to 2050, the only years the sky can be worked out for.
rules.aboveHorizonIsAltitude: aboveHorizon is true exactly when altDeg is 0 or more.
rules.aboveHorizonOnlyHeld: With aboveHorizonOnly, every star and body has an altDeg of 0 or more.
rules.magLimitHeld: With a magLimit, every star's mag is at most the magLimit.
rules.idsOnce: Each star's id and each body's id is held once.
rules.edgeJoinsHeldStars: Each constellation edge joins two different stars the reply holds.
rules.releaseOfProvider: A star's releaseVersion is its provider's: Hipparcos 2007 for Hipparcos, Gaia DR3 for Gaia DR3.
rules.sourceIdOfProvider: A star's catalogSourceId is in its provider's form: HIP and a number, or Gaia DR3 and a number.
rules.distanceInOrder: A distance's lower is at most its median, and its median at most its upper.
rules.lightTravelOfDistance: lightTravel.distancePc is the item's own median distance.
rules.astrophysicsOfGaia: Only a Gaia DR3 star has astrophysics, under its own catalogSourceId.
rules.astrophysicsHoldsAValue: Astrophysics holds a temperature or a luminosity.
rules.estimateInterval: An estimate's lower, upper and interval come together, with lower at most its value and its value at most upper.
rules.radiusFromBoth: A radius is given only with the temperature and the luminosity it is derived from.
rules.positionIsSkyPosition: A body's raDeg, decDeg, altDeg and azDeg are its skyPosition's.
rules.distanceIsInferred: A body's distancePc is its inferredDistancePc median.
rules.idsOfName: A body's id and its evidence's id are made from its name.

evidence.verificationMethod: ERFA eraPlan94 (Simon et al. 1994) for the planet and eraEpv00 (simplified VSOP2000) for the Earth and the Sun, with light time
evidence.distanceUncertaintyNote: Topocentric distance 0.795776 AU, between 0.795511 and 0.796040 AU from the method's error bounds
limitations: Predicted from the given time and place with ERFA's analytic theories; not measured in any image.
Seen from the given place at sea level (topocentric): its parallax is applied, and its right ascension and declination are astrometric (light time only).
Its altitude and azimuth are apparent and airless: refraction at 1010 hPa and 10 degrees C (Saemundsson 1986) would lift it to +51.94 degrees, and the real air differs most near the horizon.

Its uncertainty, 75.0 arcsec, adds the method's documented worst error (60.4 arcsec here), 0.00 for light deflection applied as for a star, 13.5 for UT1 - UTC taken as 0 (within 0.9 s), 0.0 for a place up to 9 km above sea level, 1 for polar motion, and 0.0 for the time scale.

The moment is UTC, later than the leap seconds announced so far (to mid 2027), so TT may be off by up to 8 s of leap seconds not yet known (ERFA calls the year dubious); UT1 is taken as UTC, within 0.9 s, if the IERS keeps it so.
